description: The Δ_λ magnitude is the trace of the sign-grading g_ρ (= ordinary dimension), a classical q=1 dimension, NOT the substrate q₀ quantum dimension. Reduces the closure to constructing g_ρ; does not derive it.
tier: symbolic-exact + mpmath (parameter-free; exact identities + q₀ q-dimension)

assertions.name: delta_lambda_is_graded_trace
assertions.detail: Δ_λ = sgn(w_0^{S_{λ'}})·dim(λ) = (q^{2n(λ)}|_{q=i})·dim(λ) = tr_{V_λ}(g_ρ) for all λ⊢6 => magnitude = ordinary dimension, NOT a separate weight ansatz

assertions.name: magnitude_is_classical_not_substrate_q0
assertions.detail: |Δ_λ|=dim(λ) is the q=1 ordinary dim; the substrate q-dimension dim_q(q₀) differs by up to 4.41% => magnitude anchor is q=1, not q₀

assertions.name: two_anchor_neither_at_substrate_q0
assertions.detail: magnitude anchor q=1 (classical dim) ⊗ sign anchor ζ₄ (grading); substrate q₀=1.109979 (real>1) is NEITHER => Δ_λ is a two-anchor object

result.verdict: MAGNITUDE REDUCED (structural; g_ρ NOT derived): Δ_λ = tr_{V_λ}(g_ρ) = (-1)^{n(λ)}·dim(λ), so the magnitude |Δ_λ|=dim(λ) is not a seventh weight-ansatz — it is the ordinary dimension carried by the SAME object whose trace gives the sign (the ρ-grading g_ρ). The magnitude is the CLASSICAL q=1 dimension, NOT the substrate q₀ quantum dimension (dim_q(q₀) differs by up to 4.41%). So Δ_λ is a two-anchor object: magnitude at q=1, sign at ζ₄, NEITHER at the substrate q₀. This REDUCES the whole Δ_λ closure to constructing the single object g_ρ (the principal ρ-grading) and pruning the substrate q-dimension. It does NOT derive g_ρ from the 13 drivers — per 'Axiomatization is NOT a Proof' the binding compute stays blocked until a driver-level construction of g_ρ exists. NOTHING wired.
